inputs.original_text: John Lahart is right to question an inheritance tax system he describes as “wholly unfair” and discriminatory against people without children. Tax rules shouldn’t assume that everyone lives within the same family structure or that those without children deserve less fair treatment. Any reform should address that inequity while ensuring inheritance tax does not simply become another route for wealth and privilege to pass between generations.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart is right that inheritance tax rules shouldn’t treat people without children as less deserving of fairness. But reform must challenge the wider inequality built into inheritance itself, not create another advantage for those able to pass wealth to relatives. A fair system should respect different family structures while making sure inherited privilege doesn’t deepen inequality or drain resources needed by everyone.
